exposure: delivery location (home, private clinics or hospitals)
delivery attendant (traditional birth attendants/community healthcare workers, relatives/others)
outcome: mother-newborn skin-to-skin contact (SSC) within the first hour of birth
cohort: The study included 11,992 ever-married women, aged 15-49 years, who delivered a live infant in Afghanistan within the past 2 years.
finding: Only 32.9% of women practiced SSC in Afghanistan, with higher likelihood among educated women, those with media access and mobile phones, and lower likelihood for home deliveries, private facility deliveries, cesarean sections, rural women, and deliveries attended by traditional birth attendants/relatives.
mod_finding: The likelihood of mother-newborn skin-to-skin contact was significantly lower in women who delivered via cesarean section [AOR: 0.12 (0.08-0.17)].
cross-section timing: Data from Afghanistan Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey (MICS) 2022-23
